title: What is personal accident insurance?

title: What is the Jeevan Jyoti scheme premium?

title: What is a pension plan in insurance?

title: What is PM Kisan?

title: What is the Direct Benefit Transfer scheme?

title: What is international banking?

title: What is a SWIFT transfer?

title: What is forex?

title: What is currency conversion?

title: What is a forex card?

answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is the Liberalised Remittance Scheme?
text: LRS allows resident Indians to remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year abroad for permitted purposes like education, travel, investment, and maintenance of relatives.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a remittance?
text: A remittance is money transferred by an NRI to their family in India. India is the world's top remittance receiver, with NRIs sending billions annually.

title: What is FEMA in banking?
text: FEMA (Foreign Exchange Management Act) governs all cross-border transactions, NRI accounts, imports, exports, and foreign investments in India.

title: What is a correspondent bank?
text: A correspondent bank in one country provides banking services on behalf of another bank in a different country, facilitating international payments and currency exchange.

title: What is IBAN?
text: IBAN (International Bank Account Number) is a standard account number format used in Europe and many countries for cross-border transfers, containing country code, check digits, and account details.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is FCNR deposit?
text: FCNR lets NRIs keep deposits in foreign currency (USD, GBP, EUR, CAD, etc.) in Indian banks, earning interest in the same foreign currency without any exchange rate risk.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a foreign currency account?
text: A foreign currency account holds money in currencies other than the home currency — like a USD account in an Indian bank — used for international trade or travel.

title: What is a nostro account?
text: A nostro account is a bank account held by an Indian bank in a foreign country in a foreign currency — used to facilitate international payments.

title: What is a vostro account?
text: A vostro account is a foreign bank's account held in an Indian bank in Indian rupees, used for trade settlements and international payments.

title: What is a loro account?
text: A loro account is a third-party perspective — when Bank A refers to the account that Bank B holds at Bank C, it calls it a loro account.

title: What is a trade finance letter of credit?
text: A letter of credit in trade finance is a bank guarantee to the exporter that payment will be made when shipment documents confirming delivery are presented.

title: What is a bank draft for international transfer?
text: An international bank draft is a bank-issued cheque in foreign currency payable at a specified foreign bank. Used for large one-time payments abroad.

title: What is a forex trading account?
text: A forex trading account with a broker allows you to buy and sell currency pairs to profit from exchange rate movements. High risk; not for average savers.

title: What is currency hedging?

title: What is a forward contract in forex?
text: A forward contract is an agreement to exchange currency at a fixed rate on a future date, protecting businesses from exchange rate risk on future transactions.

title: What is the RBI's role in forex?
text: RBI manages India's forex reserves, intervenes in the market to prevent extreme rupee volatility, and sets rules for all cross-border transactions under FEMA.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is the India-Russia Rupee Trade settlement?
text: India and Russia (and some other countries) have bilateral agreements to settle trade in Indian rupees or their own currencies, reducing dependence on the US dollar.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a packing credit loan?
text: Packing credit is a pre-shipment loan given to exporters by banks to buy raw material and produce goods before shipping. Repaid when payment from foreign buyer is received.

title: What is an export credit guarantee?
text: Export Credit Guarantee Corporation (ECGC) provides insurance to Indian exporters against the risk of non-payment by foreign buyers.

title: What is a documentary collection?
text: Documentary collection is a trade payment method where the exporter's bank forwards shipping documents to the importer's bank, releasing them only when the buyer pays or commits to pay.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is an LC at sight?
text: A sight LC requires the importer's bank to pay immediately when the exporter presents the correct shipping documents, with no credit period.

title: What is a usance LC?
text: A usance (deferred payment) LC allows the importer to pay after a set period (30, 60, or 90 days) after shipment documents are presented.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a bank guarantee in international trade?
text: A bank guarantee assures the overseas buyer or seller that if the Indian party fails to meet its contractual commitment, the bank will pay the guaranteed amount.

title: What is foreign currency non-repatriable (FCNR) vs NRE?
text: FCNR deposits are in foreign currency, protecting against exchange risk. NRE deposits are in rupees, so exchange rate applies on deposit and withdrawal.

title: What is the impact of RBI intervention in forex market?

title: What is hawala?

title: What is money laundering?

title: What is a sanctions screening in banking?

title: What is de-dollarization?

title: What is a digital currency for international payments?
text: Central banks are exploring CBDCs for cross-border transactions that could be faster and cheaper than SWIFT, reducing reliance on correspondent banking.

title: What is the special drawing right (SDR)?
text: SDR is an international reserve asset created by the IMF. Its value is based on a basket of major currencies (USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP). India holds SDRs as part of forex reserves.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is the International Monetary Fund?
text: The IMF is an international organization that provides financial assistance and policy advice to countries facing balance of payments crises, promoting global economic stability.

title: What is the World Bank?
text: The World Bank provides loans and grants to developing countries for development projects — infrastructure, education, health — to reduce poverty.

title: What is ADB?
text: Asian Development Bank (ADB) provides loans, grants, and technical assistance to Asian countries, focusing on infrastructure, energy, and sustainable development.

title: What is the BIS?
text: Bank for International Settlements (BIS) is a global institution owned by central banks that promotes international monetary cooperation and acts as a bank for central banks.

title: What is G20 and its banking relevance?
text: G20 is a forum of the world's 20 largest economies. It discusses financial regulation, tax policy, global banking rules (Basel), and economic coordination between nations.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a euro bond?
text: A eurobond is a bond issued by a company or government in a currency different from the country where it's issued — like an Indian company issuing USD bonds in London.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a masala bond?
text: A masala bond is a rupee-denominated bond issued by an Indian entity in overseas markets. Foreign investors take the currency risk, and India gets foreign funds in rupees.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is an offshore banking unit?
text: OBU is a special bank branch in India's special economic zones (SEZs) that can conduct banking transactions in foreign currencies with non-resident entities.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a free trade zone banking?
text: Banks in free trade zones or SEZs operate under relaxed regulations to attract foreign business and facilitate international trade finance.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is the rupee trade settlement mechanism?
text: India allows bilateral trade settlement in rupees with several countries. The exporter/importer gets paid in rupees instead of converting to dollars, simplifying trade.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a country risk in banking?
text: Country risk is the risk that a foreign country may default, impose capital controls, or face instability, making it difficult for borrowers to repay international loans.

title: What is a sovereign risk?
text: Sovereign risk is the risk that a government will default on its own debt or be unable to honour guarantees given to foreign lenders.

title: What is foreign debt?
text: Foreign debt is money borrowed by a government or company from international lenders in foreign currencies. Repayment becomes more expensive if the local currency weakens.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is external commercial borrowing?
text: ECB is money borrowed by Indian companies from foreign lenders in foreign currency. It's cheaper than domestic borrowing but carries forex risk. Regulated by RBI.

title: What is a foreign exchange derivative?
text: Forex derivatives (options, futures, swaps) are contracts used to hedge against or speculate on future currency movements.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is arbitrage in forex?
text: Forex arbitrage is simultaneously buying and selling currency pairs across markets to profit from tiny price differences. High-frequency computers mostly do this today.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is carry trade?
text: Carry trade is borrowing in a low-interest-rate currency and investing in a higher-interest-rate currency. Profitable in stable conditions, but risky if exchange rates move.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is the purchasing power of the rupee abroad?
text: The purchasing power of the rupee abroad depends on the exchange rate. A weaker rupee means your money buys less in foreign currency terms.

title: What is a currency war?
text: A currency war is when countries deliberately devalue their currencies to make exports cheaper, boosting trade at the expense of trading partners.

title: What is dollarization?
text: Dollarization is when a country officially or unofficially uses the US dollar as its currency instead of its own, often when local currency is too unstable.

title: What is cross-border capital flow?

answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is the impact of a strong dollar on India?
text: A strong dollar makes the rupee weaker, increasing the cost of imports (especially oil), raising inflation, but also benefiting IT and export companies that earn in dollars.

title: What is an import letter of credit?
text: An import LC is issued by an Indian buyer's bank to assure the foreign seller of payment upon shipment. It gives the seller confidence to export goods.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a bank's forex dealing room?
text: The forex dealing room is where a bank's treasury traders buy and sell currencies for the bank and clients, managing the bank's forex exposure in real time.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is FATF?
text: FATF (Financial Action Task Force) is an intergovernmental body setting global standards for combating money laundering and terrorist financing. Countries failing FATF assessments face restrictions.

title: What is the FEMA compliance for sending money abroad?

title: What is a grey list in FATF?
text: Being on FATF's grey list means increased monitoring due to strategic deficiencies in anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorism financing measures.

title: What is a correspondent banking relationship?
text: When Bank A (in India) and Bank B (in the US) maintain accounts with each other to process international transactions on behalf of their customers, they have a correspondent relationship.

title: What is the capital market?
text: The capital market is where long-term financial instruments like shares, debentures, and bonds are bought and sold. NSE and BSE are India's main capital markets.

title: What is the money market?
text: The money market deals with short-term borrowing and lending — usually under 1 year. Instruments include Treasury Bills, Commercial Paper, and Certificates of Deposit.

title: What is a Treasury Bill (T-Bill)?
text: T-Bills are short-term government securities (91-day, 182-day, 364-day) issued by RBI on behalf of the Government of India at a discount to face value.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a government security (G-Sec)?
text: G-Secs are debt instruments issued by the central government to borrow money. They pay regular interest and are considered the safest investment in India.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a corporate bond?
text: A corporate bond is a debt security issued by a company to raise funds. It pays fixed interest and the principal at maturity. Higher yield than G-Secs but more risk.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a debenture?
text: A debenture is a form of long-term debt issued by companies. It pays fixed interest and is backed by the company's creditworthiness, not specific assets.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a commercial paper?
text: Commercial paper is a short-term unsecured promissory note issued by large corporations to raise funds for working capital needs, typically for 7–365 days.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a certificate of deposit?
text: A CD is a short-term fixed-income instrument issued by banks to raise funds, similar to an FD but in standardized denominations and tradeable in the secondary market.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is the repo market?
text: The repo (repurchase agreement) market is where banks borrow short-term funds from RBI or other banks by selling securities with an agreement to buy them back at a higher price.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is call money market?
text: The call money market is where banks lend and borrow funds overnight to manage their daily cash requirements, at the call money rate.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is the primary market?
text: The primary market is where new securities — IPOs, FPOs, and new bond issues — are sold for the first time directly by the issuer to investors.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is the secondary market?
text: The secondary market is where already-issued securities are traded among investors on stock exchanges. The issuing company doesn't receive money here.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is an IPO?
text: An Initial Public Offering is when a company sells its shares to the public for the first time via a stock exchange to raise capital for growth.

title: What is an FPO?
text: A Follow-on Public Offer is when an already-listed company issues additional shares to raise more capital from the public.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a rights issue?
text: A rights issue allows existing shareholders to buy additional shares at a discounted price before they are offered to the public.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a private placement?
text: Private placement is when a company raises funds by selling securities directly to select institutional investors or HNIs, not through a public stock exchange.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a Qualified Institutional Buyer (QIB)?
text: QIBs are large institutional investors like mutual funds, FIIs, and insurance companies that are permitted to invest in certain securities due to their financial expertise.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is book building in IPO?
text: Book building is the process where the IPO price is determined by collecting bids from investors within a price band. The final price is set where demand meets supply.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a price band in IPO?
text: A price band is the minimum (floor) and maximum (cap) price within which investors can bid for shares in a book-built IPO.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is grey market premium in IPO?
text: Grey market premium (GMP) is the informal price at which IPO shares are traded before official listing. It indicates expected listing gains but is unofficial and risky.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is ASBA in IPO application?
text: ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) blocks the application money in your bank account. If shares aren't allotted, the block is released automatically.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is Sensex?
text: Sensex is the BSE benchmark index tracking 30 large, well-established companies. A rise in Sensex broadly means the Indian economy is doing well.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is Nifty 50?
text: Nifty 50 is NSE's benchmark tracking 50 large-cap companies. It's widely used for index funds, ETFs, and as a performance benchmark for fund managers.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a large-cap stock?
text: Large-cap stocks are the top 100 companies by market cap on Indian exchanges. They are more stable, well-established, and have more liquidity.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a mid-cap stock?
text: Mid-cap stocks are companies ranked 101st to 250th by market cap. They offer higher growth potential than large-caps but with more volatility.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a small-cap stock?
text: Small-cap stocks are companies below 250th rank by market cap. They can multiply in value rapidly but are high-risk and less liquid.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a sector fund?
text: A sector fund invests in companies from a specific industry — IT, pharma, banking, FMCG. High reward but concentration risk.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a thematic fund?
text: A thematic fund invests across sectors around a theme — like infrastructure, consumption, ESG, or digital economy. More diversified than sector funds.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is SEBI's role?
text: SEBI regulates and develops India's securities market — it makes rules for stock exchanges, protects investor interests, and prevents fraud and insider trading.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is insider trading?
text: Insider trading is when someone with access to non-public, price-sensitive information trades shares to gain an unfair advantage. It's illegal and penalized by SEBI.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is intraday trading?
text: Intraday trading means buying and selling shares within the same trading day. Profit depends on short-term price movements. High risk; not for beginners.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is delivery trading?
text: Delivery trading means buying shares and holding them in your demat account for more than one day. Suitable for long-term investors.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is BTST trade?
text: BTST (Buy Today Sell Tomorrow) is when you sell shares the next day after buying, before they are officially credited to your demat account.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is margin trading?
text: Margin trading lets you buy more stocks than you can afford by borrowing funds from your broker, using your existing portfolio as collateral. High risk.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is short selling?
text: Short selling means selling a stock you don't own (borrowed from a broker), expecting its price to fall, so you can buy it back cheaper and profit.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is futures trading?
text: A futures contract is an agreement to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price on a future date. Used for hedging or speculation.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is options trading?
text: Options give you the right (not obligation) to buy (call) or sell (put) an asset at a set price before a specific date. Used for hedging and speculation.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a derivative?
text: A derivative is a financial contract whose value is derived from an underlying asset — like stocks, bonds, currencies, or commodities. Includes futures and options.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a depository participant?
text: A DP is an agent of NSDL or CDSL — like a bank or broker — through whom you open your demat account. They link you to the depository.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a portfolio management service?
text: PMS is a customised investment service for HNIs (minimum ₹50 lakh) where a professional fund manager actively manages a portfolio of stocks on your behalf.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is an alternative investment fund?
text: AIF is a privately pooled fund investing in assets like real estate, private equity, hedge funds, and venture capital. Minimum investment is ₹1 crore.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a real estate investment trust?
text: REITs allow you to invest in income-generating real estate (like malls and offices) listed on stock exchanges, earning rental income without directly owning property.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is an Infrastructure Investment Trust?
text: InvITs are listed trusts that pool money from investors to invest in infrastructure assets (roads, power, pipelines), paying out regular income from project revenues.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is commodity trading?
text: Commodity trading involves buying and selling physical goods like gold, silver, crude oil, and agricultural products through exchanges like MCX or NCDEX.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is MCX?
text: MCX (Multi Commodity Exchange) is India's largest commodity derivatives exchange, where contracts for gold, silver, copper, crude oil, and other commodities are traded.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is gold ETF?
text: A gold ETF is an exchange-traded fund where each unit represents physical gold. You can buy and sell gold ETF units like shares on the stock exchange.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a liquid fund?
text: A liquid mutual fund invests in short-term money market instruments. It's safer than equity, offers slightly better returns than savings accounts, and is highly liquid — redemption in 24 hours.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is an overnight fund?
text: An overnight fund invests in securities maturing the next day. It's the safest mutual fund category and ideal for parking surplus cash for 1–3 days.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is an arbitrage fund?
text: An arbitrage fund exploits price differences between cash and futures markets. It's taxed like equity but is low risk, making it efficient for short-term parking.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is dividend reinvestment plan (DRIP)?
text: DRIP automatically reinvests dividends received from a stock or mutual fund back into more units or shares, compounding wealth without any effort.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a capital gain distribution?
text: When a mutual fund sells securities at a profit, it distributes the gains to unit holders as capital gain distributions, which may attract tax.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is a market order?
text: A market order is to buy or sell a stock immediately at the best available price in the market. Execution is guaranteed but the exact price isn't.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is the settlement cycle in India?
text: NSE and BSE follow T+1 settlement — shares bought today are credited to your demat account by the next trading day.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is STT?
text: Securities Transaction Tax is a tax levied on buying or selling of shares, mutual fund units, and derivatives on Indian stock exchanges. It's collected at source.

title: What is an algo trading?

title: What is an index ETF?

title: What is market timing?

title: What is a financial benchmark?

title: What is quantitative easing?

title: What is a bank's net worth?

title: What is tier 1 capital?

title: What is tier 2 capital?

title: What is a bank's leverage ratio?

title: What is a performing asset?

title: What is a banking ombudsman?

title: What is a credit appraisal?
text: Credit appraisal is the process of evaluating a loan applicant's ability and willingness to repay — checking income, credit history, employment, and the purpose of the loan.

title: What is a guarantor vs co-applicant?

title: What is a bullet repayment loan?

answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is an evergreening of loans?
text: Evergreening is an illegal practice where banks extend new loans to borrowers just to repay old ones, hiding NPAs. RBI strictly monitors and penalises this.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is MIBOR?

title: What is a structured product in banking?

title: What is a bank's credit rating?

title: What is window dressing in banking?

title: What is the difference between bank and NBFC?

title: What is a credit card balance transfer?

title: What is micro ATM?

title: What is digital onboarding?

title: What is the Basel Accord?

title: What is a delinquency rate?

title: What is a Wilful defaulter?

title: What is a stress test in banking?
text: A stress test simulates extreme economic scenarios to check if a bank has enough capital to stay solvent during a crisis — like a sharp rise in NPAs or liquidity crunch.

title: What is a contingent liability?
text: A contingent liability is a potential obligation that may arise depending on an uncertain future event — like a lawsuit or a bank guarantee that may be invoked.

title: What is a subordinated debt?

title: What is securitisation in banking?

title: What is a green loan?
text: A green loan is specifically used to fund environmentally sustainable projects — renewable energy, energy efficiency, green buildings, and clean transport.

title: What is ESG in banking?

title: What is financial literacy?

title: What is a moratorium in loan?

title: What is a bank's treasury?
text: The treasury department manages a bank's own investments, liquidity, forex exposure, and compliance with CRR and SLR requirements.

title: What is a correspondent account?

title: What is core capital in banking?
text: Core capital is the highest quality capital — equity and retained earnings — that a bank uses to absorb losses. It's the foundation of a bank's financial safety.

title: What is a bank consortium?
text: A bank consortium is a group of banks jointly funding a large loan to a single borrower, sharing the risk. The lead bank coordinates the consortium.

title: What is a lender's liability?
text: Lender's liability refers to legal obligations banks have towards borrowers — to act in good faith, disclose terms fairly, and not arbitrarily change loan conditions.

title: What is sub-debt issuance?
text: Sub-debt (subordinated debt) is issued by banks as bonds that pay higher interest but are repaid last in case of winding up. Used to boost Tier 2 regulatory capital.

title: What is a bank's dividend payout?

title: What is a bond yield?

title: What is a yield inversion?

title: What is an AT1 bond?

title: What is a bank's return on equity?

title: What is resolution of a failed bank?

title: What is the Financial Stability Report?

title: What is an asset reconstruction company?

title: What is bank nationalisation?

title: What is a banking sector reform?

title: What is a virtual banking licence?

title: What is a bank's net interest income (NII)?

title: What is an accretion model in banking?

title: What is a consortium lending?

title: What is auto-debit in banking?

title: What is account transfer from one branch to another?

title: What is a bank's role in money creation?

title: What is session timeout in net banking?

title: What is a payment link?

title: What is a CIBIL dispute?

title: What is a co-borrower vs co-applicant?

title: What is loan amortisation?

title: What is a loan write-off?

title: What is an anti-phishing tip?

title: What is the role of FIU-IND?

title: What is a bank inspection by RBI?

title: What is a profit and loss statement?

title: What is working capital?

title: What is free cash flow?

title: What is leverage in finance?

title: What is a financial statement analysis?

title: What is equity financing?

title: What is debt financing?

title: What is solvency?

title: What is a group health insurance by bank?

title: What is the FATCA declaration in banking?

title: What is a cross-border NACH mandate?

title: What is an open-ended mutual fund?

title: Can I freeze my account? What is the procedure to freeze / unfreeze a Demat Account?
text: Yes, the depository system provides the facility to freeze the depository accounts for debits or for both debits and credits. In an account freeze for debits, no debits will be permitted from the account till the time you unfreeze it. This is an additional security feature for the benefit of the investors. For an account which is frozen for all operations no credits or debits will take place. There is an additional feature in NSDL system which allows you to freeze a particular ISIN or part quantity of an ISIN in an investor's account.In case of freezing, the freezing date has to be mentioned i.e. the date from when the freezing of the account is sought. (No need to mention freezing end date as the NSDL system does not provide to capture the freezing "end date"). On receipt of the request, the DP will verify that the form is duly filled in, verify the signature/s of the client and thereafter, if the request form is in order the DP changes the status of the Client's account from 'ACTIVE' to 'SUSPENDED FOR DEBIT' OR 'SUSPENDED FOR ALL'. This depends on the choice of the client from the date mentioned by the client on the form. However, to unfreeze we need the freezing "end date", i.e. the date from when unfreezing of the account is sought. If the request form is in order the DP changes the status of the client's account to 'ACTIVE' on the date mentioned by the client on the form.

title: Why should I dematerialise my securities?
text: You should dematerialize you securities because:SEBI has mandated delivery of stocks only in the dematerialized form; hence if you hold physical certificates you may not be able to sell them immediately.Physical holdings need to be maintained by you and protected from loss, theft, mutilation, fire etc. In case of Demat holdings these worries are taken over by Depository Participant (DP) wherein holdings are maintained electronically by the DP in the Investors Demat Account.A transfer of Demat Holdings is a simple process and can be done by submission of a single page signed delivery instruction slip to the DP. These transfers can also be done from the convenience of your home or office through the Internet. Demat Holdings are automatically received in your Demat Accounts.Convenience of maintenance: Securities held in Demat Accounts are extremely convenient to maintain. For eg. A single request to update your address or dividend bank mandate needs to be submitted for a single Demat Account and the updated details will be applicable to all securities held in this Demat Account. Comparatively, if the securities are held in physical form you will have to submit requests individually for each company/security.The Depository System in India has become very popular and most brokers refuse to deal with physical holdings.More and more instruments are being made available to hold shares in Demat form, the latest being Mutual Fund Statement of Account (SOA). With this you can hold, view and maintain all your investment categories i.e. equity, debt, mutual funds, etc. under a single Demat Account.

title: What is FATCA/CRS/KYC?
text: FATCA : In January 2013, the United States of Americas (U.S) treasury released the final FATCA Regulations. FATCA requires U.S based financial institutions (FI) as well as foreign financial institutions to identify their U.S accounts and report them periodically to the U.S IRS (Internal Revenue Service) or appropriate governmental authority, in case of Inter-Governmental Agreement (IGA). Non-compliance can result in adverse consequences, including a penal U.S withholding tax, for non-U.S. entities or penalties under the local inter-governmental . CRS : To combat problem of offshore tax evasion, the G20 and OECD (Organisation of Economic Co-operation and Development) countries developed a Common Reporting Standard (CRS).CRS requires financial institutions to collect and report information to their tax authorities about account holders resident in other countries. India has signed CRS agreement on 3rd June 2015. UBO : As per SEBI Master Circular No. CIR/ISD/AML/3/2010 dated December 31, 2010 regarding Client Due Diligence policy, related circulars on anti-money laundering and SEBI circular No. IR/MIRSD/2/2013 dated January 24, 2013, non individuals and trusts are required to provide details of controlling persons [CP] / ultimate beneficiary owner [UBO] and submit appropriate proof of identity of such CPs/ UBOs. The beneficial owner has been defined in the circular as the natural person or persons, who ultimately own, control or influence a client and/or persons on whose behalf a transaction is being conducted, and includes a person who exercises ultimate effective control over a legal person or arrangement. As per regulatory requirement, individual investors and joint holders are required to provide extended KYC details. In absence of the same, transactions may get rejected by AMC/RTA. Joint holders of ISA ( Mutual Fund) accounts may update the same through "Update Extended KYC" option in NetBanking Request section of Accounts tab. Non-individual customers & HUFs may submit extended KYC details to Branches /Relationship manager. In absence of the same, transactions may get rejected by AMC/RTA

title: What is a Digital Certificate?
text: Digital Certificate is an electronic certificate that establishes your Identity. Digital Certificate is one of the strongest authentication mechanisms available today, as it is highly inimitable. It provides non-repudiation with tamper-evident seals, important for legal situations and has legal sanction. Digital Certificates are issued by authorized and well-defined facilities known as Certifying Authorities (C.A.), which can also to revoke, cancel or renew the certificates. In India, the regulations and guidelines mandate that Digital Certificates issued by CA be in crypto tokens for reasons of security. In India, Digital Certificate is used for Filing Income Tax Returns for Non-Individual entities, Submitting e-tenders, Filing of MCA21 (Ministry of Company Affairs), and Agent Logins for IRCTC, amongst other applications.

As far as possible, Card should be used at authorized places / centres only. Besides, PIN number should never be written on the Card.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: Whether illiterate customers can be issued RuPay Card?
text: Yes. However, Branch Manager will have to advise all the related risks to the illiterate account-holder at the time of issuance of RuPay Card.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: How to link Mobile Number with Bank Account?
text: Mobile Number of an account holder is entered in customers account in CBS System by the Bank on the basis of information given in the Account Opening Form. Also, for existing accounts, banks permit seeding through ATM, SMS from registered mobile, net-banking or on making a request in the branch (there may be variations depending on the bank).
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: How to keep debit card operational?
text: To get benefit of Accidental Insurance Cover, RuPay Debit Card must be used at least once in 45 days.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: How long is the debit card valid and how to get Debit Card renewed ?
text: Debit Card expiry date is mentioned on the Card itself. Account-holder is advised to get issued new card well before expiry date of his/her existing card by giving fresh application to the concerned bank.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: If someone has two or more accounts and two or more RuPay Debit Cards, whether accidental insurance cove is available in each account / each card?
text: Accidental insurance cover is available only in one account.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is PoS Machine?
text: PoS stands for Point of Sale. PoS Machine is a small device installed at almost all Business Centres to facilitate cashless purchases to their customers.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: Does a person already having a Bank account in any bank needs to open another account under Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojna (PMJDY) to get the Accidental Insurance Benefit under the Scheme?
text: A person who is already having a bank account with any bank NEED NOT open a separate account under PMJDY. He/she will just have to get a RuPay Card issued in his existing account to get the benefit of insurance. Credit facility can be extended in the existing account if it is being operated satisfactorily.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: If the present address is different than that of printed on Aadhaar Card, can the account still be opened under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana on the basis of Aadhaar Card?
text: If address has changed, then a self-certification of current address is sufficient.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: Whether banks will be organizing Account Opening Camps in future also?
text: Yes. Nationalized banks have been asked to organize camps on all Saturdays from 8.00 AM to 8.00 PM. Banks can hold additional camps on other days also.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: If I have required papers for issuance of Aadhaar Card, can I get Aadhaar Card in Bank and open my account under PMJDY simultaneously?
text: Aadhaar Registration may be got done in Camps organized by UIDAI. In account opening camps also, endeavor is to make Aadhaar Registration Counter available.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: Can a minor (below 18 years of age) open an account under PMJDY?
text: A minor of above the age of 10 years can open his / her Savings Bank account in any bank.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: Who is Business Correspondent Agent / Bank Mitra and what is their role in PMJDY?
text: Business Correspondent Agents (Bank Mitras) are retail agents engaged by banks for providing banking services at locations where opening of a brick and mortar branch / ATM is not viable. Scope of activities of Business Correspondents / Bank Mitra are as under: Creating Awareness about savings and other products and education and advice on managing money and debt counseling.Identification of potential customers.Collection and preliminary processing of various forms for deposits including verification of primary information /data.Filling of applications / account opening formsCollection and payment of small value deposits and withdrawals.Receipt and delivery of small value remittances / other payment instructions.Furnishing of mini account statements and other account information.Any other service on behalf of the Bank, duly authorized by the appropriate authority etc.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: Who can be Bank Mitr?
text: Banks have been permitted to engage individuals / entities as Business Correspondent (Bank Mitrs) like (i) Retired Bank Employees (ii) Retired Teachers (iii) Retired Govt. Employees (iv) Ex-Servicemen (v) Individual owners of kirana / medical/ fair price shops, individual Public Call Office (PCO) operators, Agents of Small Savings Scheme of Government of India / Insurance Companies, for profit companies registered under the Indian Companies Act. Since 24.06.2014, RBI has permitted Non Deposit taking NBFCs as BCs in addition to above.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: Can I get my PMJDY account transferred to other City / State upon my transfer posting to other States?
text: All banks participating in PMJDY are on CBS (Core Banking Solution) platform and the account can easily be transferred to any branch of the bank in any city/town as per the request of the account-holder.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: Is there any documentation to be submitted?
text: No documents to be submitted.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is the billing date and payment due date for Insta Loan / Insta Jumbo Loan / SmartEMI?
text: Same Billing Date and Same Payment Due Date as your Credit Card. For Customers availing Jumbo Loan, 2 Statements will be sent on the monthly billing date one statement for your credit card and Separate statement for Jumbo Loan Card No.
answer_label: Demo knowledge - not confirmed HDFC Bank policy

title: What is the promo code to be entered in the loan booking page?
text: Promo Code is an optional field and has to be left blank.
